newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Red Cross chief calls for Zaire military action.
newsitem.headline: Red Cross chief calls for Zaire military action.

text.p: The president of the International Committee of the Red Cross, Cornelio Sommaruga, called on Friday for Western military intervention to help aid agencies gain safe access to one million refugees in east Zaire.
"There is no other option," he told Reuters after a news conference on the humanitarian crisis, when asked if he thought Western military intervention was needed.

Sommaruga, speaking at the news conference, appealed to the U.N. Security Council to urgently take necessary measures and said chapter seven under the U.N. charter which authorises member states to use military force, was not ruled out.
"There is an extreme urgency. The victims cannot wait any longer. Time is passing," Sommaruga said. "These people have a right to international assistance and protection."

"There are means that can be used. It's up to the international community to make the choice and see to it that humanitarian agencies are able to act," he said. "Global political solutions are needed in this region."

The ICRC chief said his agency and other relief organisations were ready to go into eastern Zaire if their basic security was assured. "We had to quit the region because of pillage, looting and chaos, not because of the conflict," he said.
